What it measures: Which controller backup this sample was recovered from.
Watch out: The CS9 log is cumulative, so a newer backup contains older samples too. Duplicates were removed.

What it measures: Application run number. Increments once each time the app starts.
Watch out: Blank on samples from before the run counter existed.

What it measures: Production run time since the last RESET. Excludes operator-hold time.
Watch out: Not wall-clock. The cell can be powered and idle without this advancing.

What it measures: Plates picked since the last RESET.
Where it comes from: Counted on the rising edge of Pick3 linear retreat — the same event the PLC ladder counts.

What it measures: What the cell was doing at the instant the sample was written.
Watch out: FAULT on the last sample of a run usually just means the operator ended it with the Abort button.

What it measures: Run time divided by plates. The headline rate.
Watch out: Dragged down by every loss, so it is always worse than the cell's capability. Compare against Fastest clean s.

What it measures: Same figure as rate per hour.
The budget. 2.965 s.
Watch out: Constant on every row.

What it measures: How far over budget each plate runs.
Watch out: This is the number to drive to zero.

What it measures: Actual rate as a share of the 1,214 pl/hr target.
Where it comes from: Formula: Actual pl/hr ÷ B6 on this sheet.
Watch out: Recalculates if you change the target in B6.

What it measures: Least Repeatable Cycle, 10th percentile. A pessimistic floor for what the cell repeats.
Where it comes from: Upper edge of the histogram bin holding the 10th percentile of clean cycles.
Watch out: Suppressed below 10 clean cycles — a tenth percentile of nine samples is not a percentile. Pessimistic by up to one bin, never optimistic.

What it measures: The quickest uninterrupted plate-to-plate interval measured.
Watch out: The cell's demonstrated capability. The gap between this and Actual s/plate is losses, not capability.

What it measures: Mean of the clean intervals only.
Intervals where no loss bucket moved.
Intervals where something did interfere.
Watch out: A high count with a good LRC means the cell is capable but keeps being stopped.

What it measures: Share of intervals that were clean.
Watch out: Rising clean % through a run is the cell settling in.

What it measures: Time the arm was actually picking or placing.
Watch out: Not waste — but it is where the time is once the other buckets are small.

What it measures: Indexing the feeder to bring the next parts into view.
Watch out: Cost per plate falls as plates per advance rises, so read it beside Plates/advance.

What it measures: Belt running with nothing arriving.
Where it comes from: Belt time beyond nStarveSec in one episode.
Watch out: Upstream supply, not a cell problem.

What it measures: Waiting because the accept station was full.
Waiting because the reject station was full.
Arm idle waiting on the camera.
Where it comes from: Gap time that ended in a pick.
Watch out: Near zero here — the capture is hidden behind concurrent motion. A faster camera would buy almost nothing.

What it measures: Time in a genuine fault.
Where it comes from: bERROR["schunk"] only, since the Aug 31 split.
Watch out: Before that split this bucket also caught the abort button, which made whole runs read 100% fault.

What it measures: Time no bucket claimed.
Where it comes from: Pending gap written off after nPendMax.
Watch out: This is the partition's self-test. If it grows, a state is missing from the model.

What it measures: Abort routine active, or parked waiting for the operator to choose Cycle or Stow.
Watch out: Deliberately outside the rate: it is downtime, not slow production. Blank before this column existed.

What it measures: The eight partition buckets added up. Operator hold is deliberately NOT one of them.
Where it comes from: Formula on the data sheet: Productive through Unattributed.
Watch out: Should equal Actual s/plate. Operator hold is excluded because it sits outside run time — adding it would break the check by exactly the hold figure.

What it measures: Validation residual.
Watch out: Should be 0.000. Anything else means the data is misaligned or the partition is incomplete.

What it measures: How many plates one belt advance yields.
Watch out: Doubling this halves belt cost per plate without the belt getting any faster.

What it measures: Number of belt advances.
Where it comes from: Counted on entry to the belt state.
Watch out: Consecutive fruitless passes count as one episode.

What it measures: The worst single belt episode.
Watch out: A large value with low Plates/advance is a starving feeder.

What it measures: Mean time per OCCURRENCE of each motion phase. The sixteen phases below are the arm cycle split at the setMoveId() calls in PartPick and PartPlace.
Where it comes from: _nPhSec[i] / _nPhCount[i] in tkMetrics. The phase is picked from bRobotMotion[...], which tkGetMoveID sets from getMoveId() bands.
Watch out: PER OCCURRENCE, NOT PER PLATE — accept phases run only on accepted plates, reject phases only on rejected ones. For per-plate: × occurrences ÷ Plates. They also do NOT sum to the cycle: moveId 900 and the 400s/550s/650s/800+ ranges are in no band, and the abort move (700–749) has a flag but no ph index.

What it measures: Nothing. No move in the deployed build is tagged in this band.
Where it comes from: moveId 50–99. There is NO setMoveId() in that range anywhere in the deployed project.
Watch out: ALWAYS BLANK, and that is not a data gap. StowSelect_Pick0_Fix (Aug 31) adds setMoveId(50) to tkCycle for the stow-select wait, but it was never deployed — the 15h07 backup has no 50–99 setter. Blank on all 15 samples. The 'Wait at capture' label on the Cycle Data sheet describes the intent, not the running code.

What it measures: movej to the belt pick approach pose, arm empty.
Where it comes from: PartPick setMoveId(100) → movej(pBelt_START, tGripper, mBlend). pBelt_START = jointToPoint(tGripper, world, jBelt["start"]).
Watch out: For tie plates that point is then multiplied by pPoseTransform (the Apera pose offset), so the target — and this duration — moves with where the plate is lying. Spike and Anchor skip the transform.

What it measures: The Apera trajectory down onto the plate, ending with the gripper closing.
Where it comes from: PartPick setMoveId(200) → apera2:apera_exec_traj("LINEAR_APPROACH", mFAST) then waitEndMove(). Waypoints come from Apera, not from a stored point.
Watch out: Also contains tTool("ON") and dDoComply_xyz=false, so it is motion PLUS gripper actuation dwell. Longest pick phase at ~1.15 s, and roughly half of that is the tool, not the move.

What it measures: The Apera trajectory lifting the gripped plate clear of the belt.
Where it comes from: PartPick setMoveId(250) → apera_exec_traj("LINEAR_RETREAT", mFAST), with dDoComply_xyz=true restored first, then wait(getMoveId()>=250 and <300).
Watch out: THIS IS THE CYCLE BOUNDARY. tkMetrics counts a plate on its rising edge — the same edge the PLC counts on X114 — so Plates, LRC and every per-plate figure on this sheet key off this one phase.

What it measures: movej out to the belt exit pose with the plate held.
Where it comes from: PartPick setMoveId(300) → movej(pBelt_END, tGripper, mBlend). pBelt_END = jointToPoint(tGripper, world, jBelt["end"]), × pPoseTransform for tie plates.
Watch out: OVER-REPORTS. PartPick then sets moveId 900, which is in NO band, so tkGetMoveID leaves this flag TRUE until PartPlace issues setMoveId(500). The dead time between the pick finishing and the place starting is charged here, so read ph4 as 'retreat plus handover', not as travel.

What it measures: movej into the accept station with the plate held.
Where it comes from: PartPlace accept branch, setMoveId(500) → movej(pPlace_AcceptEND, tGripper, mBlend). Target is jAccept["end"] × pPoseTransform.
Watch out: Named START but the target is the station's END pose — the very point ph9 returns to. jAccept["start"] is computed in PartPlace and then never moved to, so nothing measures it.

What it measures: movej to the standoff 50 mm above the accept drop point.
Where it comes from: setMoveId(510) → movej(appro(pPlace_Accept, trZ["50mm"]), tGripper, mBlend). pPlace_Accept = jAccept["pos"] × pPoseTransform.
Watch out: Uses mSlow instead of mBlend when the station was full (bAccept_Overflow), so a hold inflates this phase as well as filling the Accept hold bucket — the two are not independent.

What it measures: movel the last 50 mm down onto the accept drop, then release the plate.
Where it comes from: setMoveId(520) → movel(pPlace_Accept, tGripper, mNomSpeed), then waitEndMove() and tTool("OFF").
Watch out: Contains the gripper-release dwell, which is why it is the longest place phase at ~0.7 s. mSlow on an overflow hold.

What it measures: movel straight back up to the 50 mm standoff, arm now empty.
Watch out: The cleanest phase on the sheet — one short linear move, no tool action, no vision. Useful as the reference when judging whether another phase is slow.

What it measures: movej back out to the accept station END pose, arm empty.
Where it comes from: setMoveId(540) → movej(pPlace_AcceptEND, tGripper, mBlend) — the same point ph5 came in to.
Watch out: OVER-REPORTS like ph4: the flag stays true after PartPlace returns until the next setMoveId — 100 for the next pick, or 750 for a capture move — so the inter-cycle gap is charged here.

What it measures: movej into the reject station with the plate held.
Where it comes from: PartPlace reject branch, setMoveId(600) → movej(jReject["start"], tGripper, mBlend).
Watch out: Moves to the JOINT target directly, so the Apera pose transform is NOT applied here — unlike the accept side. n/a on every sample: Accept % is 100% and nothing has been rejected yet.

What it measures: movej to the standoff 50 mm above the reject drop point.
Where it comes from: setMoveId(610) → movej(appro(pPlace_Reject, trZ["50mm"]), tGripper, mFAST). pPlace_Reject = jReject["pos"] × pPoseTransform.
Watch out: mSlow on a reject-station overflow hold. Blank on every sample so far.

What it measures: movel the last 50 mm down onto the reject drop, then release the plate.
Where it comes from: setMoveId(620) → movel(pPlace_Reject, tGripper, mFAST), then waitEndMove() and tTool("OFF").
Watch out: Reject uses mFAST where the matching accept phase (ph7) uses mNomSpeed, so ph12 and ph7 are NOT comparable. Blank on every sample so far.

What it measures: movel straight back up to the 50 mm standoff, arm now empty.
Watch out: Blank on every sample so far.

What it measures: movej out to the reject station exit pose, arm empty.
Watch out: Joint target, no pose transform. Over-reports like ph4 and ph9. Blank on every sample so far.

What it measures: movej back to the camera capture pose over the belt, arm empty. Runs only when vision returned no trajectory.
Where it comes from: tkCycle's else branch, setMoveId(750) → movej(jBelt["capt"], tGripper, mBlend), then delay(nLoopPace).
Watch out: ONE OCCURRENCE PER FRUITLESS VISION PASS, not one per plate — so its occurrence count is the no-trajectory count. Longest phase on the sheet (1.5–2.6 s) and it is the belt-advance transit, which is why Belt advance and ph15 move together.

What it measures: Plates sent to each station.
Share accepted.
Watch out: 100% on every run to date.

What it measures: Plates by part type.
Where it comes from: Apera pick-point ID mapped to part class.
Watch out: Only 14-inch tie plates have run so far.

What it measures: Mean duration of one trajectory capture.
Watch out: High here with Vision wait near zero means the look is hidden behind motion. Read the two together or you will chase the wrong thing.

What it measures: Number of trajectory captures.
Where it comes from: Counted on the rising edge of the trajectory flag.

What it measures: Fastest tool-centre-point speed seen.
Watch out: A peak, not an average.

What it measures: Share of run time the arm was below nStopMMS.
Watch out: Standing still is not always waste — the gripper has to close.

What it measures: Share of run time the arm was moving.
Share of the pick phases with the arm stationary.
Watch out: Mostly gripper actuation and waitEndMove handshakes. Now measured directly as tTool dwell.
